User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the AssetPro application.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of when the user account was last updated.

Property.title: Property
Property.description: Represents a property managed within the AssetPro application.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this property. (Relationship: User 1:N Property)

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the property was added.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of when the property was last updated.

Tenant.title: Tenant
Tenant.description: Represents a tenant renting a property.

propertyId.description: Reference to the Property being rented. (Relationship: Property 1:N Tenant)

moveInDate.description: Date when the tenant moved in.

moveOutDate.description: Date when the tenant moved out (if applicable).

Agreement.title: Agreement
Agreement.description: Represents a lease agreement between a property owner and a tenant.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant associated with this agreement. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Agreement)

documentURL.description: URL of the lease agreement document.

startDate.description: Start date of the lease agreement.

endDate.description: End date of the lease agreement.

rentAmount.description: The rent amount specified in the agreement.

terms.description: Terms and conditions of the lease agreement.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Represents an expense associated with a property.

propertyId.description: Reference to the Property associated with this expense. (Relationship: Property 1:N Expense)

categoryId.description: Reference to the ExpenseCategory for this expense. (Relationship: ExpenseCategory 1:N Expense)

ExpenseCategory.title: ExpenseCategory
ExpenseCategory.description: Represents a category for expenses (e.g., maintenance, utility, tax).

id.description: Unique identifier for the expense category.

Report.title: Report
Report.description: Represents a generated report for a property or set of properties.

userId.description: Reference to the User who generated the report. (Relationship: User 1:N Report)

propertyIds.description: References to the Properties included in the report. (Relationship: Property N:N Report)

generationDate.description: Date when the report was generated.

reportDataURL.description: URL to access the generated report data (e.g., PDF or JSON).

aiInsights.description: The AI insights included in the report.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to manage properties, tenants, agreements, expenses, and reports for the AssetPro application. The structure prioritizes authorization independence and supports secure list operations through path-based ownership and structural segregation. User-owned data is stored under `/users/{userId}` to simplify security rules and ensure data privacy. Specifically, properties, tenants, agreements, and reports are stored as subcollections under each user's document. This design ensures that only the user can access their own data.

**Authorization Independence:** The design achieves authorization independence by ensuring that access control is based solely on the `request.auth.uid` and the path. There are no `get()` calls required to determine ownership. Each user's data is isolated under their respective user ID, making security rules straightforward. For instance, only the authenticated user matching the `userId` can access data under `/users/{userId}`.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** The structure supports secure `list` operations by leveraging path-based ownership. Listing properties under `/users/{userId}/properties` is secure because the rule only needs to check if `request.auth.uid == userId`. This prevents unauthorized access and ensures that rules do not act as filters.

**Structural Segregation:** Data is segregated based on ownership. Each user's properties, tenants, agreements, expenses, and reports are stored in separate subcollections under their user document. This ensures that data with different access needs (e.g., one user's properties vs. another user's properties) are not mixed in the same collection, simplifying security rules.
